key_insight: Aiding buoyancy suppresses vortex shedding near a heated square cylinder but drives a plume-like instability farther downstream.
engineering_relevance: Thermal-flow designs must account for buoyancy stabilizing the near wake while potentially generating downstream oscillations.
method: Two-dimensional DNS across Reynolds and Richardson numbers, including extended downstream domains.
Local plume scaling and mixed-convective correlations for flow and heat transfer.
Linear stability analysis of the two-dimensional base flow.
evidence_signal: Linear stability analysis reproduces both transitions as Hopf bifurcations and accurately predicts DNS frequencies and finite-domain thresholds, while local plume scaling improves collapse of far-field instability onset.
watch_item: Results are based on two-dimensional simulations, and far-field transition thresholds depend on the downstream distance available for disturbance growth.
paper_title: Buoyancy-induced transitions in mixed convective flow past a heated square cylinder
